name: Quercetin

lead: Quercetin is a plant flavonol abundant in onions, capers and apples, sold as a supplement. It is also the 'Q' in the dasatinib plus quercetin senolytic combination studied in aging research.
Human evidence for benefits is limited and mixed, covering blood pressure, allergy and inflammation. Cosmetic benefits have not been established.

paras: Quercetin has antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activity and stabilizes mast cells in laboratory studies. In senolytic research it is paired with dasatinib to clear senescent cells in preliminary human work. Oral bioavailability is low.
Usually well tolerated at supplemental doses; high doses may cause headache or stomach upset and could affect kidney function or drug metabolism. Legal as a supplement.
